title: The divine laws in destroying the oppressors
summary: Editorial on the divine patterns governing the destruction of wrongdoers. It argues that Allah has fixed, unchanging historical patterns (sunan) by which tyrannical and disbelieving nations are brought to ruin, applying equally to past nations and present ones. Drawing on Quranic verses about the sudden destruction of arrogant communities, it sets out the sequence: wrongdoers are granted respite and grow arrogant, are gradually lured toward ruin, fall into internal discord and failure, and are finally seized, often destroyed at the hands of the believers or by being set against one another. The editorial applies this schema to its contemporary enemies, naming the West ('Crusaders'), Israel ('Jews'), and the Shia ('apostate Rafida') as oppressors whose present dominance is temporary and divinely doomed. The piece is consolatory and morale-oriented, reframing the current strength of IS's adversaries and any setbacks as a transient phase within an inevitable divine pattern.
keyClaims: Allah has fixed, unchanging historical patterns by which oppressive and disbelieving nations are destroyed.
Tyrants are granted respite and grow arrogant before being seized suddenly and brought to ruin.
The destruction of wrongdoers often comes at the hands of the believers or by setting enemies against one another.
The current dominance of the West, Israel, and the Shia is temporary and subject to this divine pattern.
significanceAssessment: A consolation and morale editorial reassuring supporters that the present strength of IS's enemies is transient and their downfall divinely ordained. Reframes military pressure and setbacks as a phase within a longer providential pattern, reinforcing endurance. Identifies the West, Israel, and the Iran-aligned Shia as the wrongdoers destined for destruction.
